sections.h2: Does Tennessee have a homestead exemption on property tax?
sections.html:
Tennessee does not give owners a homestead exemption that removes part of a home's value from the tax roll. What it offers instead is a state reimbursement program called property tax relief, plus a local option tax freeze. The Comptroller describes relief as a reimbursement, and a court of appeals case noted in the statute annotations says the relief statute is not an exemption statute at all: the property stays taxable and the city and county receive the full tax.

Tennessee also has a separate homestead rule in Title 26 that protects equity from creditors. People often confuse the two, and a seller dealing with both a tax bill and a debt may need to look at each one. This page covers the tax programs first and the creditor protection after that.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for Tennessee property tax relief in 2026?
sections.html:
Low-income homeowners who are 65 or older, homeowners who are totally and permanently disabled, and certain disabled veterans or their surviving spouses can qualify. The program began in 1973 and is paid from state appropriations. You apply through the county trustee, or the city collecting official if the property is inside a city.

  • Elderly: you must be 65 on or before December 31 of the application year, own the home, and use it as your primary residence.
  • Disabled: you must be disabled on or before December 31 of the application year, with the same ownership and residence tests.
  • Disabled veteran: you must complete a 2026 Form F-16, which releases disability and income information from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
  • Surviving spouse of a disabled veteran: you must complete Form F-16S, provide a death certificate and personal ID, and not have remarried.

The income that counts is the combined income of all owners, the applicant's spouse, and any resident owner of a remainder interest. A sole owner within $100 of the cap, or a household with a co-owner within $200 of the cap, must document income from every source. Social security, railroad retirement and veterans benefits that must be paid to a nursing home are not counted for an owner who moves into one.

sections.h2: When and where do I apply for relief?
sections.html:
You apply when your 2026 tax bill arrives, and the deadline is 35 days after the local delinquency date. Because delinquency begins March 1, that deadline falls in April. The Comptroller's schedule shows the same April date, and local officials forward applications to the state, which normally expects them by May 5.

A county trustee can give a credit on the bill if the application looks eligible, provided you pay the balance. Statute does not require the whole bill to be paid by the delinquency date as a condition of eligibility, though the brochure tells applicants that taxes must also be paid by the deadline, so confirm with the trustee how your county handles it. The director of the Division of Property Assessments may waive a missed deadline for good and reasonable cause, but never past December 31 of the year after the tax year.

You can check an application's status on the Comptroller's website, or call the Property Tax Relief office at 615.747.8871. The office sits in the Cordell Hull Building in Nashville.

sections.h2: How does the Tennessee property tax freeze work?
sections.html:
A freeze locks the tax on a principal residence at the amount owed in the first year the owner qualifies. Afterward the amount generally stays the same even if the rate rises or the county reappraises. The General Assembly passed the Property Tax Freeze Act in 2007, and each county or city chooses whether to adopt it.

  • You must own your principal residence in a participating county or city and be 65 by the end of the year you file.
  • Your income from all sources must stay under the limit for your county, and you reapply every year with proof of income, age and ownership.
  • The freeze covers the home and no more than 5 acres. Taxes on commercial, farm or forest portions are not frozen.
  • If the actual calculated tax falls below the frozen amount, you pay the lower amount and the frozen figure resets downward.
  • The benefit adds to the relief program, but it requires its own application.

The Comptroller counted 28 counties and 37 cities on the 2026 list. Local option limits are tied to a $60,000 base set for 2024 and moved by the Social Security cost of living adjustment, reaching $63,470 for 2026.

Sample 2026 income limits from the Comptroller's freeze list: Davidson, Knox and Shelby counties and the city of Chattanooga $63,470; Williamson County $69,150; Madison County $51,620.

sections.h2: What happens to relief or a freeze when I sell?
sections.html:
The freeze does not travel with you. The Comptroller says the base amount changes when an owner sells and buys another residence, and benefits must be established separately for each property. Improvements to the home raise the frozen base in proportion to the added value.

For the freeze, you do not need to have owned the home on January 1, but you must have owned it for part of the year and still own it on the application deadline. If a qualified applicant dies mid-year, taxes stay frozen for the whole year. Under the relief statute, a surviving spouse can present a voucher chosen by a deceased applicant and receive the final payment, unless the taxes were paid before the death.

Relief is limited to one residence and one recipient per property for each tax year. A person who gave false income information must repay the state, with penalty and interest. Someone paid in error generally must repay if the state makes demand within two years of the due date for that tax year. Before listing, ask the trustee whether you have a pending voucher or credit on the parcel so that closing figures match.

sections.h2: What does the $35,000 state homestead protect?
sections.html:
Tennessee Code section 26-2-301 lets an individual protect up to $35,000 of homestead equity from creditors, and joint owners claiming together can protect $52,500. A 2021 amendment raised those amounts from $5,000 and $7,500, effective January 1, 2022. The General Assembly's fiscal memorandum on SB 566 and HB 676 also raised the amount of sale surplus exempt for a surviving spouse or minor children from $5,000 to $35,000.

The same amendment removed the higher tiers that once existed for owners 62 or older and for owners with minor children. The memorandum adds that, under section 26-2-306, homestead exemptions do not apply to property tax liens. A tax bill is therefore outside what this protection reaches.

This creditor protection comes into play when a lender or other creditor goes after the house. It has no application form like the tax programs do. An attorney can tell you how it interacts with a mortgage, a judgment or a bankruptcy filing.

faqs.q: Is there a Tennessee homestead exemption that lowers my property tax?
faqs.a: No. Tennessee's closest program is property tax relief, which reimburses taxes after you pay them, and the local tax freeze, which caps the amount owed. Neither removes value from the assessment. The $35,000 state homestead only protects equity from creditors and does not apply to property tax liens.

faqs.q: How much income can I have and still get 2026 relief?
faqs.a: The 2026 Comptroller brochure sets the limit at $38,470 for elderly and disabled homeowners, based on 2025 income for the applicant, spouse, co-owner and resident remainder owner. Relief is figured on up to $33,600 of market value. Disabled veterans and qualifying surviving spouses have no income limit.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply?
faqs.a: Apply within 35 days after the local property tax delinquency date, and pay your taxes by that deadline as the brochure instructs. Since delinquency starts March 1, the cutoff lands in April. The state director can waive a missed deadline for good cause until December 31 of the following year.

faqs.q: Can I use the freeze in any county?
faqs.a: Only in counties and cities that adopted it. The Comptroller's list shows 28 counties and 37 cities, and each has its own income limit for 2026. Ask your county trustee or city collecting official whether your address is covered.

faqs.q: Does the homestead protect me from unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: No. The fiscal memorandum for the 2021 amendment points to section 26-2-306, which makes homestead exemptions inapplicable to property tax liens. Contact the county trustee about the balance on your parcel.
